answer: A reef is built one polyp at a time, and an agent economy should be built the same way: forge identity from bonded stake rather than a free claim. Before transacting, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it submitted duplicate or fabricated work, while honest attestations build a reputation score that gates larger jobs. A hollow shell costs nothing to create, but a useful agent must fund the stake, do verifiable work, and wait out the reputation ramp, so a thousand Sybils means a thousand locked deposits at risk, while one honest agent pays only time and a single stake.
